articles.title: El 'skater' madrileño Danny León, primero en grindar el larguero de una portería de fútbol
articles.standfirst: El atleta de Red Bull y deportista olímpico protagonizó un 'world first' sobre una de las porterías del estadio Metropolitano
articles.summary: El atleta de Red Bull y deportista olímpico protagonizó un 'world first' sobre una portería de fútbol
articles.body: El 'skater' madrileño Danny León, atleta de Red Bull y deportista olímpico en Tokio 2020 y en París 2024, protagonizó un 'world first' con el que se convirtió en la primera persona en recorrer con su monopatín el larguero de una portería de fútbol profesional. El reto, ejecutado en colaboración con el Atlético de Madrid, se llevó a cabo en el estadio Metropolitano y contó con la participación de Marc Pubill, jugador del club rojiblanco y campeón del mundo con la selección española en el Mundial de Estados Unidos, México y Canadá, informó en un comunicado Red Bull. Este nuevo hito convirtió una portería reglamentaria de fútbol, de 7,32 metros de ancho y con un larguero situado a 2,44 metros de altura, en un raíl de 'skate' de más de siete metros. Para alcanzar la velocidad necesaria, Danny se impulsó mediante un 'winch', un sistema conectado a un cable al que se sujetaba durante el recorrido. Courage Adams, atleta de BMX de Red Bull, fue el encargado de accionar el sistema mediante un mando y controlar el impulso para que Danny llegara a la rampa con la velocidad y trayectoria precisas. La acción contó también con la presencia del internacional colchonero Marc Pubill, que siguió el reto desde el terreno de juego. "Este proyecto es muy especial para mí porque une dos de mis grandes pasiones: el fútbol y el 'skate'. De pequeño iba a los entrenamientos de fútbol patinando, con las botas de tacos puestas, así que poder grindar una portería en un estadio como el Riyadh Air Metropolitano es un sueño hecho realidad", explicó Danny León. El pasado 12 de agosto, León aprovechó el eclipse solar en España para inmortalizarse haciendo un salto en uno de los momentos más espectaculares de este fenómeno astronómico, cuando la luna tapaba completamente el sol. "El truco de mi vida", reconoció el propio deportista en la publicación de Instagram donde subió el vídeo de esta hazaña, que se viralizó en las redes sociales logrando millones de reproducciones y convirtiéndose en una de las imágenes más icónicas del eclipse. Danny León es uno de los grandes referentes españoles del 'skate' de 'park' y 'bowl', con un extraordinario historial en el festival de O Marisquiño, en Vigo, llegando a representar a España en los Juegos Olímpicos de Tokio 2020 y París 2024.

articles.body: Former four-division world champion Adrien Broner is facing a criminal trespass charge after authorities allege he returned to a Florida casino despite receiving a lifetime ban. The case involves the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino, where police say Broner was arrested after an alleged trespass incident in April 2024. A court has now issued a warrant connected to the case, adding another legal problem for the former champion.Broner has not publicly responded to the trespass case. Broner has denied those accusations.Why is Adrien Broner facing a trespass charge?According to the Seminole Police Department report by TMZ, officers were called to the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino in April 2024 following an alleged trespass. Police say Adrien Broner had already been issued a lifetime ban from the property in August 2023.Authorities allege that Broner returned to the casino despite the ban. The incident eventually led to an arrest and a criminal trespass charge. The case has remained unresolved for a lengthy period, and a warrant was recently issued for Bronerâs arrest.No further details about the alleged incident have been made public. Broner has yet to respond to the charge.The latest case adds to a difficult period for the former boxing champion. articles.body:
Former England footballer Raheem Sterling ⁠has ⁠been charged with dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide for ⁠wrongful inhalation following a motorway crash in May, say Hampshire ⁠Police in the United Kingdom.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous ‌driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen,” a Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesperson said in a statement ⁠to Reuters news agency on Wednesday.

He is due to appear at a magistrates’ court on September 15 for a hearing.

Sterling, who most ⁠recently played for Dutch side Feyenoord, crashed his Lamborghini into barriers on the ⁠M3 motorway. No other vehicles were involved and ⁠no injuries were reported.

Sterling, ⁠who joined Feyenoord on a short-term deal in February after leaving Chelsea by ‌mutual consent, has been without a club since the end ‌of ‌last season.

articles.title: Could Erik Karlsson join Toronto Maple Leafs after Elliotte Friedman sparks fresh NHL trade rumors for 2026-27
articles.summary: NHL News: Fresh NHL trade rumors suggest that defenseman Erik Karlsson could potentially join the Toronto Maple Leafs for the 2026-27 season. With his impressive track record, including winning three Norris Trophies, Karlsson could provide Toronto with the offensive boost they need from the blue line as he enters the final year of his contract with the Pittsburgh Penguins.
articles.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs have already made big changes to their roster this offseason in a bid to reshape it for the 2026-27 NHL season, and there is no confirmed trade between the two teams at this time, but the latest speculation involving Erik Karlsson adds another potential blockbuster to the mix.That is notable because Karlsson is still a very good NHL defenseman, as Friedman noted, and the three-time Norris Trophy winner could provide Toronto with more puck-moving as well as offensive production from the blue line if the Pittsburgh Penguins make him available.Could Erik Karlsson join Toronto Maple Leafs this NHL season?Erik Karlsson may become a Toronto Maple Leafs trade target in the 2026-27 NHL season, but for now, itâs all speculation, not an actual trade report.Elliotte Friedman recently speculated that Karlsson could end up in Toronto while discussing potential developments around the NHL. The idea is picking up steam because the veteran defenseman is entering the last year of his current contract with the Pittsburgh Penguins.Friedmanâs projection is not an implication that Pittsburgh is actively shopping Karlsson, or that Toronto has entered into formal trade talks. Instead, it puts the Swedish defenseman among the names to watch as the season progresses.Why would Toronto Maple Leafs consider Erik Karlsson?Karlsson would fill Torontoâs need for a second experienced offensive defenceman. The 36-year-old has been known for elite puck movement, skating and playmaking from the blue line throughout his career.His offensive game is still there. As Karlsson showed in the 2025-26 NHL season, he can still be a difference-maker in the twilight of his career, with 66 points in 75 games for the Pittsburgh Penguins.Heading to Toronto would also provide the Maple Leafs with another veteran presence who can move the puck quickly and create offence at five-on-five and on special teams.The biggest hurdle may be Karlssonâs contract and Torontoâs salary cap. His current contract carries a $11.5 million cap hit per year, so any trade would be financially tricky.Toronto would likely need similar salary to take him off the roster or for Pittsburgh to retain some of Karlssonâs contract. The Leafs would also have to weigh whether adding an expensive veteran defenceman fits into their broader plan for building a roster.For the Pittsburgh Penguins, it may come down to where they are in the standings. If Pittsburgh is still in the race, it may be better to keep Karlsson around. His expiring deal could make a trade more likely if the Penguins struggle and become sellers.When could Toronto Maple Leafs pursue Karlsson?It will be easier to get a read on a potential Karlsson trade once the 2026-27 season starts. Early returns could show if Pittsburgh is in the playoff hunt and if Toronto needs another big piece on the blue line.For now, Elliotte Friedmanâs comments should be viewed as a fun bit of NHL trade rumour mill activity, not an indication that a deal is imminent. The Karlsson-to-Toronto storyline is one to watch as both teams figure out where they are headed this season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Vote. The Republic's top 2026 high school girls cross-country athletes
articles.summary: Here is The Arizona Republic's list of top 25 girls high school cross-country athletes for the 2026 season. Vote in our poll for the top runner.
articles.body:
The 2026 Arizona high school cross-country season officially has arrived.

The Arizona Republic is previewing the top cross-country athletes in the state. These are the top 25 girls runners in Arizona, regardless of division. The rankings are based on performances from the 2025 cross-country season, as well as the 2026 spring track and field season.

ALA Queen Creek senior Tally Call has been in the mix at the top for years and now seeks to claim the top spot in Arizona, but a handful of runners stand in the way, including an impressive crop of youngsters. Gilbert Highland will attempt to tie Phoenix Xavier Prep's AIA record with a sixth consecutive Division I team state championship — and the Hawks have all the tools to do so.

We have included a poll asking readers to vote for the top athlete (the poll appears after the list; print readers can find it with this story online at azcentral.com/sports/high-schools ).

The Republic's top 25 girls cross-country athletes in 2026

The fastest returner in Arizona for the 5,000 at 18:19.7. She has helped lead ALA Queen Creek to three straight team state championships since she was a freshman and now looks set for individual glory this fall.

2. Natalia Morris, Gilbert Highland, Jr.

She could end the season at No. 1. The next great runner in a long line of them at the school. Ran 18:39.3 in the 5,000 last fall and 10:53.88 in the 3,200 in the spring.

3. Cassidy Long, Mesa Mountain View, So.

Coming off a breakout freshman season, where she ran 18:39.4 in the 5,000 and 10:47.81 in the 3,200. She's got a lot of potential.

4. Gwen LeVander, Waddell ALA West Foothills, Jr.

She became the first from the LeVander Family to win a state title — cross-country or track and field — this past year, taking home the Division III crown. Ran 11:03.57 in the 3,200 during track.

5. Isabella Cropper, Phoenix Pinnacle, Sr.

One of only five returning athletes who has broken 11:00 in the 3,200 (10:54.88). Has a best of 18:57.4 in the 5,000. Could be a dark-horse candidate to win the individual title in Division I.

With her training partner, Tally Call, the two form one of the fastest lead packs for any team in the state. Personal best of 18:22.9 in the 5,000.

7. Katelyn Anderson, Gilbert Highland, Jr.

Arguably displayed the most growth on last year's title-winning team, shaving off nearly two minutes in the 5,000 (19:20.8) to become a contributing scorer.

She's dealing with a bit of an injury, but will be back to full health soon. Will be one of the athletes pushing the pace for the Hawks.

9. Emerson Butler, Phoenix Country Day School, Jr.

She's showing that it doesn't matter if you're from a small school — if you're fast, you're fast. Her time of 10:51.66 in the 3,200 makes her the second fastest returner in the state. Last year's Division IV runner-up.

10. Taelyn Janssen, Waddell Canyon View, Jr.

She could become the next Janssen to win a state title. After watching her sister, Taryn, win an individual state title and her brother, Tanner, win a team state title at Glendale Prep, Taelyn is trying to reach the same heights at Canyon View. Has run 19:06.5 in the 5,000 and 11:13.39 in the 3,200.

11. Sydney McCracken, Glendale Mountain Ridge, Sr.

Ready to attack the season after an "amazing" block of summer training, according to coach Mitchell Moses. Personal best of 18:47.1 in the 5,000.

After consecutive third-place finishes at the last two state championships, she's "motivated this year more than ever."

13. Kendyl Taylor, Phoenix Desert Vista, Jr.

Desert Vista has a rich history of distance running and Taylor could be the next to carry that mantle. The 800-meter specialist has run 18:48.1 in the 5,000.

14. Allison Reamer, Cave Creek Cactus Shadows, Sr.

One of the top runners in Division II. She has finished 15th, eighth and fifth at the past three state championships. This could be the year for her.

15. Sawyer Lemieux, Queen Creek Crismon, So.

She raced like a veteran as a freshman, finishing 35th overall at last year's championships in the merged results. Already close to breaking 19:00 in the 5,000 (19:04.7).

One of the most impressive freshmen from last year, part of what could be a very special class. Showed a lot of improvement, going from 22:42.8 (elevation) to 19:52.1 in the 5,000.

17. Rhima Edkaidek, Tempe Corona del Sol, Sr.

Performs when it matters most: her personal best in the 5,000 (19:34.8) came at the state championships.

She's expected to be a major contributor for Pinnacle this season after a breakthrough on the track, running 11:13.75 in the 3,200. Gets to train with one of the top runners in the state, Isabella Cropper.

She will look to build on her strong spring. Was a top 50 finisher in the merged results at last year's state championships.

20. Sylvia Harding, Cave Creek Cactus Shadows, Sr.

With her teammate, Reamer, pushing it, the two have each other to work off. She's a very consistent runner.

21. Tylee Salcido, Gilbert Williams Field, So.

Don't be surprised if there's a big jump in performance from her. Got down to 19:12.2 in the 5,000.

22. Mara Mellberg, Chandler Hamilton, Sr.

Transferred from Chandler Valley Christian in the winter and quickly fit into the Hamilton program under coach Mike Scannell, running 11:18.0 in the 3,200.

23. Chantel Newman, Phoenix Xavier Prep, Sr.

Established herself last season and now looks to step into a lead role for the Gators, with the departure of Kennedy Frakes. Has run 19:20.0 in the 5,000.

On the cross-country course, she is a championship racer. Has worked her way up in Division III, finishing 10th last year.

25. Savannah Koontz, Tucson Salpointe Catholic, Sr.

One of the top runners from southern Arizona. Coach Aleta Jokisch said Koontz has looked "strong and is running well" over the summer.

articles.title: FSU football season preview: New faces, new expectations
articles.summary: After a 5-7 record in the 2025 season, FSU looks to bounce back with new players, including redshirt senior quarterback Ashton Daniels.
articles.body:
After Florida State football conquered the University of Alabama 31-17 in last year's season opener, the Seminoles appeared poised for a strong season. However, after going winless on the road for the second consecutive season, FSU finished 5-7. This marked the fourth time in six seasons the 'Noles failed to qualify for a bowl game under head coach Mike Norvell.

With over 57 new players, there are numerous individuals looking to make an immediate impact, including redshirt senior quarterback Ashton Daniels, freshman linebacker Izayia Williams, junior linebacker Chris Jones, and redshirt senior kicker Gabe Panikowski. The Garnet and Gold now look not to erase the past, but to learn from it and apply those lessons to their 2026 campaign.

"I think we had a lot of self-inflicted wounds [last year]," senior wide receiver Duce Robinson said at the 2026 Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) Media Day press conference on July 15. "This year … I think we have all of the talent in the world … we're hungry to prove we are much better than everyone is projecting us."

Daniels is a high-volume passer with the ability to navigate out of the pocket and create opportunities on the run. He had limited action in the 2025 season, appearing in four games for Auburn University, but best displayed his dual-threat ability against No. 16 Vanderbilt University and No. 10 Alabama.

Between the two games, Daniels combined for 612 passing yards with a completion rate of 59 percent on 83 attempts. He also notched 197 rushing yards on 41 attempts. Daniels is looking to bring that same poise as Florida State's starting quarterback for the 2026 season.

"I know I believe in myself," Daniels said at a press conference on Aug. 13. "I have the confidence in myself to go out there and even when I'm not playing well, to flush it and continue to build on that and make better plays."

Williams is a former four-star prospect who is coming off a torn ACL ahead of his high school senior season. In 2024, he notched 125 tackles, four sacks, and one interception. With room to be a starter, Williams earned a selection on ESPN analyst Billy Tucker's "51 freshmen poised to make an impact during the 2026 college football season" list .

"[Williams] very first rep: speed, explosive, violent," Norvell said at a press conference on July 29. "He's got the skill set, the traits. He definitely looked the part in the first day of pads."

Chris Jones looks to bolster Seminole defense

Jones, a transfer from Southern Mississippi University, ranked seventh in total tackles with 134 last season. He is a sideline-to-sideline run stopper, which will be crucial for a Seminoles defense that surrendered an average of 214.6 rushing yards per game in its last three games of 2025.

"I feel like this year we have more intensity, more strength to the ball," Jones said at a press conference on Aug. 11. "[Linebacker] coach [Ernie] Sims says all the time, 'solve your mistakes with violence,' and that's what we try to do every day; [we] try to fly to the ball as a unit."

A fresh leg for Florida State's special teams

Panikowski did not appear in a game last season, but brings proven accuracy to Tallahassee, as the kicker went 15-for-15 on field goals with a career long of 55 yards for Idaho State University in 2024. The fifth-year transfer placekicker is looking to bolster FSU's special teams unit, which ranked second to last in the ACC in field goal efficiency last season, converting 12-of-19 attempts.

"Preparation creates confidence, and I can say with certainty that I have prepared myself for this opportunity," Panikowski said at a press conference on Aug. 13. "One snap, one hold, [and] one kick at a time."

The 'Noles possess what ESPN considers the hardest strength of schedule in the ACC and the 22nd hardest schedule in the nation. The Garnet and Gold will face marquee matchups against Alabama, Clemson University, the University of Florida, and the 2025 national champion runner-up University of Miami.

"We understand the expectation," Norvell said at the ACC Media Day press conference on July 15. "There's no person or place that has higher expectations than we have being part of this program; making sure we're doing things the right way, the Florida State way, competing for championships, in all things that we do."

Florida State kicks off its 2026 season against New Mexico State University at Doak S. Campbell Stadium on August 29 at 7 p.m.

Hunter Milligan is a Senior Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com.

articles.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy shares his progress working with Rashee Rice
articles.summary: During Tuesday's press conference, Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy shared his progress working with Rashee Rice | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy spoke with reporters before practice on Tuesday. He shared his progress with wide receiver Rashee Rice as the team prepares for the 2026 season.

"Well, first of all, Rashee (Rice) is a very good player. His overall resume has spoken for itself. The thing I'm trying to get to know, and we're still working through this, is getting to know the person," said Bieniemy. "To see the things that make him click. What are the things that inspire him? What are some of the things that he loves to do off the field? It's all about building relationships with people. And so the thing that I love about Rashee, first and foremost, he's tough. He's very, very tough. Another thing, and I'm not saying this in a bad way, he's hardheaded."

The Chiefs are looking forward to having Rice for a full season after he missed multiple games last year due to suspension and injuries. Bieniemy is focused on getting the best version of Rice this season under his coaching.

"He's stubborn because he feels that he's good enough at certain things, and I like that because you got to get him to see it from a different point of view. And when he can see it from a different point of view with a set of different eyes, now it opens up his brain," said Bieniemy. "And I mean, you can see it resonate, and so those are the things that I've learned about him. Now, it's just about making sure we can get the continuous reps to get him back on track, to get him in game shape because we have to get it right. And on top of that, we got to make sure that all the little fine details that need to be executed are basically done within the next couple of weeks or so."

Rice finished last season with 53 catches for 571 yards and five touchdowns, averaging 10.8 yards per reception.

articles.title: More than a coach: Bobby Bowden’s impact on Florida State University
articles.summary: Views staff writer Connor Davis writes that Bobby Bowden’s tenure at Florida State helped the university, the student body, and Tallahassee.
articles.body:
Bobby Bowden built more than a football program: he built an entire world through it. Often, Bowden is remembered for his success as a football coach; while his accomplishments are great, he did not only win national championships. Bowden built Florida State University into a worldwide brand and an image of resilience. During his tenure at the University, attendance rose and demand and funding spiked, leading to the argument that his best accomplishments were off the field.

Bowden arrived in Tallahassee in 1976 , when Florida State was not known as extensively as it is today. The Seminoles had only won four games in the three seasons before his arrival, and Bowden's first season ended with five wins and six losses. This was not the standard Bowden had; this became his only season with more losses than wins at Florida State throughout his 34-year career . While success through winning games was great, he understood that it required adversity to be noticed. He often scheduled games against major schools to get Florida State on television and he raised the bar to help with recruiting.

The effect Bowden created was extremely clear, especially through student interest. Bowden said that when he first arrived in Tallahassee, FSU had struggled to fill its residence halls. After four years at the school, Bowden's 1981 team had been to back-to-back Orange Bowls, a nationally known, prestigious game. At an awards ceremony in 2011, Bowden said that FSU received double the amount of applications than students they could accept.

"Just because our football team had been successful and had been on national television and had gotten into a major bowl. Our president said that," Bowden said at the ceremony. Eric J. Barron was FSU's president in 2011.

This growth is important: it shows how Bowden was able to use football to build the school around him, and how it brought students to Tallahassee not just for athletics, but for academics.

Florida State's enrollment data reflects the school's transformation during the period. The University had 22,424 students in 1980, 28,237 in 1990, and 34,477 in 2000. Enrollment increased by more than 12,000 students from the start of Bowden's tenure to the year 2000, nine years before he left the school. For reference, that is a 54% increase in 20 years. Bowden's success within the University also helped the city of Tallahassee grow . The city grew from 81,548 residents in 1980 to 124,773 in 1990 and 150,624 in 2000, and growth in the 80s alone increased the population by 53%.

The school's own football stadium, Doak Campbell Stadium , is also a strong reflection of the changes that happened when Bowden first arrived in Tallahassee and the stadium only held about 40,000 people . Just over 20 years later, in 1997, it held about 80,000 people. The stadium doubled in size during Bowden's time, which is a strong reflection of the growth of the university, city, and community during his tenure. This stadium is now broadcast on national television and hosts major events like the Savannah Bananas and Professional Bull Riding .

The argument is not that every student, resident, or growth of the community is directly due to Bowden's success; obviously, there are capital and other economic factors, as well as laws, that influence these topics. The main point is that Bowden made a little-known school a nationally-known brand and gave the school a new identity that needed to be known. Due to the attention, the entire institution was able to flourish from the stems Bowden grew.

Bobby Bowden did not just build a winning program; he helped build a school, city, and community that needed support. His influence on recruiting, income for the school and city, enrollment, attendance, and higher standards across the University's programs changed the future of Tallahassee. Bowden truly put the Garnet and Gold on the map and made the Seminoles' symbol known worldwide.

Connor Davis is a social work major at Florida State University and a Staff Writer for the Views section of the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com .

articles.title: Austin Hill to drive No. 33 car for Richard Childress Racing in 2027
articles.summary: Austin Hill will drive the No. 33 car full-time for Richard Childress Racing during the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season.
articles.body:
Austin Hill is finally NASCAR Cup Series bound. On Monday, Richard Childress Racing announced that Hill will drive the No. 33 car full-time during the 2027 Cup Series season. The Richard Childress Racing driver replaced Kyle Busch in the ride after his tragic death from health issues in late May.

Hill has been running the renumbered No. 33 car for Richard Childress Racing since Busch's death, while staying in the No. 21 car in the NASCAR O'Reilly Series. Now, instead of finding a new driver for the 2027 season, Richard Childress Racing is moving forward with Hill next to Austin Dillon.

It has been a difficult battle for Hill and Richard Childress Racing, as Busch's death rocked the organization and the sport. Now, Hill will be the full-time replacement for the two-time Cup Series champion. Over the rest of 2026, Hill and Richard Childress Racing will honor Busch while preparing for the 2027 campaign.

articles.title: Amanda Anisimova seeks US Open redemption with new mindset
articles.summary: Amanda Anisimova discusses her mental health journey and her renewed focus on winning a Grand Slam at the US Open.
articles.body:
American tennis star Amanda Anisimova prepared for a press conference at the 2026 Cincinnati Open, like she's done countless times throughout her decade-long career. But this time, she was met by a sea of empty chairs.

This press conference wasn't like the others. It was a Pure Leaf "break conference."

"I thought I was walking into a press room and was going to do my usual, tending to work," Anisimova recalled to USA TODAY Sports. "And (Pure Leaf) ended up surprising me with my mom and my dog, which I had missed... I kept texting my mom like, 'Oh, I wish I could see you guys.' So that was an unreal experience."

The two-time Grand Slam finalist is heading into the 2026 US Open, the fourth and final major of the year that Anisimova "looks forward to the most," with a new perspective of what it takes to be at her best. She's used her platform to advocate for mental health, proving that stepping away sometimes helps you move forward.

"One of the most important things in life is taking a break and how important it is to reset, not just for your body, but also for your mind," Anisimova said. "It taught me everything about how important it is to have a good balance on and off of the court. And if you're not happy on the court or off of the court, then you're not really going to get the results that you want."

Anisimova spoke to USA TODAY Sports ahead of the US Open through her partnership with Pure Leaf Iced Tea, who's showing how meaningful breaks can be a game changer. Pure Leaf is also offering that opportunity to fans, hosting a Tea Break Cart near Bryant Park on Wednesday, Sept. 2, with mocktails and merch available.

Amanda Anisimova: US Open title 'would mean the world'

Anisimova announced she was stepping away from tennis in May 2023, citing burnout and mental fatigue. Anisimova dropped to No. 373 in the WTA rankings during her eight-month hiatus, but climbed to a career-high No. 3 ranking after a breakout 2025 season. She made back-to-back finals appearances at Wimbledon and the US Open, but jubilation was soon followed by heartbreak.

Anisimova lost to Iga Swiatek by a double bagel in the 2025 Wimbledon final and suffered a straight-set defeat to Aryna Sabalenka in the 2025 US Open final, despite forcing a second-set tiebreak.

The New Jersey native said the losses still linger in her mind, but staying "present and mindful" has helped her focus on small, day-by-day steps so she doesn't dwell on what could've been.

"I do get flooded with the memories of the final last year and how close I was to achieving my dream," Anisimova told USA TODAY Sports. "I'm really trying to reset and come back to the little things that I need to do day in and day out. And those are the things that I feel like help me get to the final."

Anisimova said winning her first Grand Slam title "would mean the world to me."

"That's a big goal of mine, not the only goal I have in tennis, but that's kind of like the first step of one of the biggest goals," she revealed. "I have won two 1000 tournaments (2025 Qatar Ladies Open, 2025 China Open), which were other goals that I had. And now that I've achieved those, I feel like the next one is winning a Grand Slam. But yeah, I feel like hopefully when the day comes, I'm really able to celebrate myself and with all the people around me because it really does take a village to get to that place."

Amanda Anisimova among top US contenders

Anisimova opened the 2026 US Open with mixed doubles alongside partner Learner Tien. The American duo was defeated in the first round by fellow American duo Emma Navarro and Tommy Paul, 5-3, 4-2. Although Anisimova hoped to make it further in the event, she said mixed doubles is about soaking in the atmosphere.

"I love it. I mean, I was born in New Jersey, so I have a lot of Jersey fans that come out and support me, but also the New Yorkers. It's always the best time. I love competing here and I love the crowd," she said. "I feel like I thrive off of the energy so much here. So yeah, really excited to get started."

The U.S. women are sending a strong contingent to New York. Five American women are Top 25 in the WTA rankings – Jessica Pegula (3), Coco Gauff (4), Anisimova (10), Iva Jovic (16) and Madison Keys (24).

"I think being able to share that with fellow countrywoman and countrymen that are around you playing makes it seem like you're a little bit more on a team," Pegula told USA TODAY Sports. "This sport is so individuals that I think it's kind of nice to have that feeling that we're all kind of in it together. And I think it also alleviates some pressure. There's not just one person, one American that has to win the U.S. Open."

Gauff was the last American woman to win the U.S Open in 2023 . Pegula finished runner-up in 2024 and Anisimova finished second in 2025, both behind back-to-back champion Aryna Sabalenka .

"Losing in a final definitely teaches you a lot of lessons and you're always leaving the match with some takeaways and I for sure learned a few," Anisimova added. "I've also gained experience. I mean, if I'm in that position again, hopefully I'd love to obviously be in the final again this year."

articles.title: Beau Stephens becomes important to Seahawks after Mason Richman injury
articles.summary: Rookie blocker Beau Stephens becomes important to the Seattle Seahawks after the Mason Richman injury.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks lost one rookie and one sophomore to season-ending injuries in the Week 2 preseason loss to the Tennessee Titans . Most notably, second-round safety Bud Clark suffered a broken ankle injury . Also, sophomore guard Mason Richman was placed on season-ending IR with an injury of his own.

Both injuries deliver a significant blow to the Seahawks' roster depth. Losing Richman makes rookie guard Beau Stephens even more important . The Seahawks are thinner at guard without Richman, and it could eventually force Stephens into a bigger role.

The Seahawks will start Grey Zabel and Anthony Bradford at guard for a second consecutive season. Richman was initially in the mix for a depth role behind them. With him landing on season-ending IR, Stephens and Christian Haynes are the unquestioned reserve guards.

Some even wondered if Haynes would be traded or released this offseason. That's also unlikely to happen following Richman's injury. Meanwhile, Stephens has been listed as Zabel's backup at left guard on the unofficial depth chart.

Having Richman gave the Seahawks another option at reserve guard. His absence could force Stephens and Haynes into bigger roles on the depth chart. A rookie fifth-round pick, Stephens has to be ready for whatever.

articles.title: Klay Thompson eyes 'redemption season' after move to Miami
articles.summary: Klay Thompson is eager to return to the postseason after the Dallas Mavericks finished with a 26-56 record a season ago.
articles.body:
Following his move to the Miami Heat , former Golden State Warriors guard Klay Thompson gave his thoughts on the newest chapter of his career. After signing with the Mavericks ahead of the 2024-25 season, things never went to plan for Thompson in Dallas , as the infamous Luka Doncic trade changed the team's outlook entirely. After averaging a career-low 11.7 points per game for the Mavericks in what ended up as a 26-56 season last year, the four-time champion felt it was time to move on.

Now in South Beach, Thompson has his sights set on a bounce-back season. In his introductory press conference with the Heat, Thompson said , "It's kind of a redemption season for me to show I can still make an impact on winning and do it consistently."

The former Washington State guard also revealed how much he missed playing in the playoffs, saying , "I just missed out on the postseason. I hate watching from home."

"That's all I want to do these next couple of years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run."

With a new look Heat roster that includes Giannis Antetokounmpo , Miami seems destined to improve on a 10th-place finish in the Eastern Conference last season.

articles.title: RB Trey Benson goes unclaimed, reverts to injured reserve
articles.summary: The fate of running back Trey Benson has been decided, as no team claimed him off waivers.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals announced that they waived running back Trey Benson with an injury designation. He went unclaimed off waivers, which means he is back with the Cardinals, but has reverted to injured reserve.

What usually happens in these situations is that a player will eventually be paid an injury settlement and released from IR.

Usually, players waived in this fashion are on the mend from an injury. Benson had not practiced since before the Cardinals' first preseason game. After missing most of last season with a knee injury, from which he tried to come back from late last season and failed, he had his knee flare up again in training camp.

He is technically on the Cardinals, but his time with them is over.

It is a sad end to the promise he had as a third-round pick out of Florida State in 2024.

In two seasons, he played in 17 games and rushed for 451 yards and a touchdown, averaging 4.9 yards per attempt.

Let's get the new signings right and move on.

Andy : With the exceptions of Bernardo Silva and Rodri , City's outgoings could fairly be described as fringe players, the majority of whom they have made a profit on. To get two young but already proven talents like Anderson and Bouaddi in return seems like good business.

Sean : Pep had stated previously that he felt the overall squad was too big. However, we have lost players in key positions without really replacing them. My biggest concern is the lack of depth in defence. Ake, Akanji and Stones have gone and, with no new defensive players brought in, we need one more I believe. We appear to be looking for a replacement for Marmoush which is wise. As for the overall squad, change was inevitable with Pep leaving and we will need time to bed new players in.

Liam : Not concerned by a 'fire sale', these are fringe players that haven't made the grade, and allowing space for new (and hopefully better) signings and our home grown players like Rico Lewis and Nico O'Reilly to get real chances to establish themselves in the team. This is the chance now for Hugo Viana to show his value as director of football and stamp his mark on the squad. Let's hope he can live up to what Txiki created for Pep!

articles.title: Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez offered to Chelsea
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso and Unai Emery are at Stamford Bridge and Villa Park, respectively. Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as the W...
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso and Unai Emery are at Stamford Bridge and Villa Park, respectively. Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as the West London club assesses a late-window opportunity to strengthen their goalkeeping department, according to The Athletic .

Representatives for the Argentina international have formally approached Stamford Bridge executives to gauge their interest in a deal.

Aston Villa are open to sanctioning the departure of their long-serving goalkeeper following a major reshuffle in Unai Emery's squad hierarchy.

After investing €35 million to sign Japanese international Zion Suzuki from Parma, Emery has installed Suzuki as Villa's new first-choice goalkeeper for the 2026/27 season.

This leaves Martinez facing an unfamiliar back-up role at Villa Park, prompting the club to facilitate a transfer to manage their wage bill and avoid squad friction.

The World Cup-winning goalkeeper had previously expressed a desire for a new challenge, but a proposed move to Juventus collapsed earlier in the window when the Italian club failed to meet Villa's financial demands.

With the transfer deadline fast approaching, Martinez's representatives are actively canvassing top European clubs, presenting Chelsea with a rare opportunity to land a proven, elite-level goalkeeper at a modest fee.

Chelsea's goalkeeping department is widely considered a weak spot, and the current number one, Robert Sanchez , struggled in Monday's 3-2 win over Fulham .

Since joining Villa from Arsenal in 2020, Martinez has become one of the Premier League's most commanding goalkeepers, playing a key role in Villa's consistent European qualification.

His elite shot-stopping and vocal leadership would give Chelsea an authoritative presence between the posts.

While Chelsea have not yet submitted a formal bid to Aston Villa, internal discussions continue as the club weighs the financial and sporting merits of a deal.

With Villa eager to resolve Martinez's future, talks between Stamford Bridge chiefs and the player's representatives could accelerate quickly as the window draws to a close.

articles.title: Liverpool push for Ismaila Sarr after Minteh setback: £50m bid in, Palace player wants Anfield switch

articles.body:
Liverpool have turned their attention to Crystal Palace 's Ismaila Sarr as the Reds look to sign a winger before the deadline.

Liverpool have made an offer worth around £50m for the Senegal international , after deciding against pursuing Brighton 's Yankuba Minteh .

Andoni Iraola 's side saw two bids for Minteh rejected, the last of which was around £60m. Minteh is also currently sidelined until October after undergoing ankle surgery.

Sarr has emerged as an alternative with optimism that a deal can be done. Fabrizio Romano has reported that Liverpool have lodged a £50m bid for the 28-year-old, who is keen on the move. Galatasaray had also been chasing a deal for Sarr and have had two offers turned down.

Sarr scored 21 goals in all competitions for Crystal Palace last season and was named Europa Conference League Player of the Season as the Eagles won the trophy. He then netted four times for Senegal at the 2026 World Cup this summer.

Palace are under no pressure to sell with Sarr contracted until 2029. However, the player's desire to play Champions League football and Liverpool's offer could tempt the South Londoners into a sale.

Sarr would represent a natural right-sided winger for Liverpool, following the loss of Mohamed Salah . Interest in Sarr comes alongside the pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain 's Bradley Barcola , with Liverpool keen to sign both players before the deadline.

Sarr boasts a brilliant goal record against Liverpool. He's scored seven times in 10 appearances against the Reds in all competitions for Palace and former club Watford.

articles.title: Ex-Arsenal Ramsdale requests Southampton u21 appearance
articles.summary: Former Gunner Aaron Ramsdale requested the chance to play for the Southampton u21s earlier this month, according to the club’s manager.Photo by George Wood/G...
articles.body:
Former Gunner Aaron Ramsdale requested the chance to play for the Southampton u21s earlier this month, according to the club's manager.

On August 14th, Aaron Ramsdale started for the Southampton u21s in a Premier League Cup match against Blackburn Rovers.

The match went very well, with the former Arsenal goalkeeper keeping a clean sheet in a 4-0 victory for the u21 side. But it obviously raised the question of why the 28-year-old was involved at all.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckhert provided the answer to the Daily Echo this week.

"He (Ramsdale) asked for minutes," Eckert said . "I have to say that he's been very professional from the very first day.

"We've had a conversation early on, and since I came in I've worked with Daniel [ Peretz ] and with Longy ( George Long ). We've been very clear about the situation. Daniel has signed as a number one and Longy as a number two for us going into the season. I've had that conversation with Rambo.

"I also told him he would get everything from us in the pre-season to get him in the best condition possible. It speaks for him that he wants to play.

"He just wants the feeling because there are some things that you just can't replicate in a training session."

Whilst the positive outing for the u21s will have been good for Ramsdale's fitness and confidence, he's still in a scenario where he has no realistic route to minutes with Southampton this season.

The goalkeeper had a relatively busy campaign in 2025/26, playing on loan with Newcastle United . He made 23 appearances in all competitions, but the club ultimately decided not to take up their purchase option.

If Ramsdale wants to play senior football this season, he likely needs to secure a transfer before next Tuesday's deadline. Arsenal will be watching on, knowing they hold a sell-on clause for the goalkeeper.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders’ brother Shilo takes high road after Browns’ Deshaun Watson decision
articles.summary: Shilo Sanders says Shedeur Sanders will get his opportunity.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have named Deshaun Watson their Week 1 starting quarterback, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the team's backup.

While sharing his decision with the browns fans, head coach Todd Monken said the decision followed an evaluation of the quarterbacks' "full body of work." He assessed it throughout the offseason and NFL preseason.

What surprised everyone was that the decision came after Shedeur delivered an efficient showing against Buffalo. Sanders completed 9 of 11 passes for 74 yards and a touchdown, while Watson went 5 of 12 for 36 yards with an interception.

Despite the outcome, Shedeur's brother Shilo Sanders urged people to keep the bigger picture in mind. "It's a long season," Shilo said. "Shedeur eventually is going to get his time to shine, whether it's this year, next year, it don't matter."

Shilo also refused to criticize Watson after the Browns' decision. "We never preying on nobody's downfall, and we wish the best for everybody," he said.

"You're never going to succeed if you have bad intentions in your heart and your mind," Shilo added. "If you wish bad on somebody else, bro, no matter what the situation is, that's not how you succeed."

Shedeur Sanders still has a clear path forward

Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Monken praised Shedeur's response to losing the quarterback competition. "He was awesome," Monken said. "You talk about somebody that really understands the long game."

He then added, saying, "We met this morning for a good long time, and all he had was a smile on his face because he understands."

That mindset matters for Cleveland because the quarterback situation remains far from settled. Watson is returning from a major injury and struggled against Buffalo, while Sanders showed accuracy and command during his preseason opportunity.

From a roster perspective, the Browns have reasons to give Watson the opening assignment. His $230 million fully guaranteed contract carries major financial weight, and Cleveland needs to determine whether he can regain his previous level.

Still, Sanders' development gives the Browns a meaningful alternative if Watson struggles. He enters the season as QB2, but his preseason efficiency and familiarity with the offense could matter later.

At the same time, Sanders' response gives Cleveland another reason to trust his development.

Tyson Fury has begun training camp in Miami, Florida, as he prepares for a showdown against fellow British heavyweight Anthony Joshua, according to Fury's promoter Frank Warren.

The status of the fight remained in limbo, especially after Fury recently said it "doesn't look like it is going to happen," following ongoing disagreements over the venue. Although both teams have agreed in principle to a November date, the dispute over location continues.

Both British former world champions have made it clear they would prefer to stage the fight in London, ideally at Wembley Stadium. However, the ongoing delay stems from the preference of Saudi-owned fight organizer Sela to host the event in the United States.

"I genuinely think it will happen," Warren told Sky Sports . "I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. Well, that's not quite right, they could refuse to fight. But then we don't get the fight that everyone wants to see.

"They are professional boxers; I'm not going to make any excuses about it. Would I like to see it, would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they're in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America," Warren said.

articles.title: Austin FC transfer Jayden Nelson to Bolton Wanderers
articles.summary: By Justin RudermanTRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: TransferAustin FC have transferred forward Jayden Nelson to English Championship side Bolton Wanderers, the club a...
articles.body:
Austin FC have transferred forward Jayden Nelson to English Championship side Bolton Wanderers, the club announced Wednesday.

The 23-year-old Canadian international departs for up to $2.325 million ($1.1m guaranteed, $1.225m conditional) and a sell-on fee.

Nelson recorded 2g/1a in 13 MLS appearances during his sole season with Austin. He was acquired last December from Vancouver Whitecaps FC .

A Toronto FC homegrown, Nelson has produced 5g/10a in 81 regular-season games spanning five different MLS seasons. He's also played in Europe for Rosenborg BK (Norway) and SSV Ulm 1846 (Germany).

"Jayden expressed a desire to make a move to Europe at this stage of his career, and his transfer to Bolton is a great outcome for both clubs as well as for Jayden," said Austin interim head coach Davy Arnaud .

"We wish him nothing but the best for his time in England and our leadership group felt that accepting this offer continues our efforts to strengthen the club's position as we look to the future."

Internationally, Nelson has scored three goals in 16 caps for Canada . He featured at the 2026 FIFA World Cup during his country's historic run to the Round of 16.

Austin are 14th in the Western Conference (21 points) and have made the Leagues Cup quarterfinals. Longtime Philadelphia Union head coach Jim Curtin is set to take over for the 2027 season.

articles.title: ‘I’m going to throw him out of the ring’: Filip Hrgovic send ominous warning to Moses Itauma
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic believes his maturity as a man and fighter set him apart from Moses Itauma.
articles.body:
As Filip Hrgovic nears his Aug. 29 title fight against Moses Itauma he sits down with DAZN to talk a bit about the fight, the matchup, and the difference in personas between the two, and his expectations for himself in the fight. Check out some excerpts of what he had to say below.

Hrgovic on being the betting underdog in this fight against Itauma

"I don't care. Opinions is like, everyone has it…I don't care what everyone thinks. It doesn't matter…It's just important what I think. I think I'm going to throw him out of the ring."

On how he's feeling heading into this fight

"I feel great. I feel great camp and I feel great."

On whether Itauma can still have a good career if he loses this fight

"I think the best for him would be if he lose this fight. That would be the best for him as a fighter and as a person because he's young, and if he wins titles so young he's going to ruin his life and his soul and he wouldn't be able to handle that pressure. I'm different kind of animal and I'm 35. I've been through life, through a lot of things in my life so I can handle it much better. And for him to be world champion at 21, it'll be too much for him.

"It's best for him to lose this fight and to build his career again step by step…The most important in life is to save your soul. If you don't save your soul, nothing else matters."

"I think he's just immature. He's just a kid, man. It's not a offense, it's just a reality. When I see him, I see a kid, someone who's just young. We all have been young and stupid and when you get old you change your opinion, you change your attitude…I see a kid, that's it. So, it's not his fault."

On Itauma's best chance being to get him out early

"He's like dangerous in early rounds, I'm more dangerous in late rounds — on paper it's like this. But in the fight anything can happen. I can take him out in first round or he can take me out in round 12, so you never know how the fight going to be. So we will see."

articles.title: Do the Titans have to keep RB Julius Chestnut?
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans reserve running back Julius Chestnut is once again battling for a 53-man roster spot.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will have a joint practice with the Chicago Bears on Thursday. They'll then play the preseason finale versus those same Bears on Saturday. Approximately 24 hours later, general manager Mike Borgonzi will be tasked with finalizing his initial 53-man roster.

Among Borgonzi's bigger decisions is at running back. The Titans are expected to roster four ball carriers. Tony Pollard , Tyjae Spears , and rookie Nicholas Singleton are locks.

Kalel Mullings , Julius Chestnut , and Michael Carter are competing for that fourth and presumed final spot at running back. Mullings has the benefit of being a sophomore draft pick who also plays special teams. He hasn't been healthy though, and Chestnut is beginning to capture momentum.

Chestnut leads all Titans running backs in rushing through two preseason games, and it's not particularly close. The former Sacred Heart standout has gained 95 yards via 13 attempts. He's averaging an impressive 7.31 yards per game, and ripped off a big 34-yard gain.

Chestnut has also added three receptions for 24 receiving yards to his offensive totals. He's consistently a preseason stud for the Titans. Nothing has changed this year, with Chestnut totally dominating the preseason again.

Chestnut is also an experienced special teams player. Some believe Mullings, a former college linebacker, has the edge on special teams. He may possess more upside on special teams, but coordinator John "Bones" Fassel trusts Chestnut, too.

Pollard and Spears will be the Titans' bellcows once regular-season football arrives. Chestnut could add depth and experience, though. He's a potential short-yardage back, and if the oft-injured Spears were to miss time, you'd like to think Chestnut is more trustworthy than the rookie Singleton, who is struggling in pass protection.

Chestnut is once again dominating the NFL preseason. The Titans have big-time roster decisions coming, with Carter, Mullings, and D'Ernest Johnson contending for Chestnut's roster spot.

articles.title: Kinley Rasmus breaks LLWS hits record for a girl, a day after notching her second strikeout record
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus continues to etch her name in the Little League World Series record book.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus continued her dominant run at the Little League World Series on Tuesday with another tournament record as her Phenix City, Alabama, team advanced from another elimination game.

A day after tying the total strikeouts records for a girl in the Little League World Series, Rasmus broke the tournament's record for most hits by a girl. She did so with a fifth-inning single that put runners on the corners in a 4-2 win for Phenix City over Tacoma, Washington.

The hit was Rasmus' fifth of the tournament to claim the record as her own. And Phenix City advanced while eliminating Tacoma.

On Monday, Rasmus made LLWS history on the mound — for the second time.

Rasmus struck out six to help lift Phenix City past West Chester, Pennsylvania, 6-5, in their elimination game Monday. The two-way star has compiled 14 total strikeouts in the tournament, which again matched Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts by a girl in tournament history.

Rasmus struck out eight in Phenix City's first game at the Little League World Series last week, which also tied a single-game record Davis set in 2014.

And thanks in part to Rasmus, Phenix City rallied out of a five-run hole on Monday night. Rasmus threw more than four scoreless innings after coming in for relief to help spark the rally. It marked the team's second straight elimination win.

Rasmus is the daughter of former MLB pitcher Cory Rasmus and the niece of former MLB outfielder Colby Rasmus . Cory is an assistant coach for Phenix City this summer, and both brothers played on Phenix City's 1999 Little League World Series team.

Rasmus is one of two girls playing in the tournament this year. Carsynn Meyer is playing for Paseo Verde (Nevada). They are among the 25 girls who have competed in the event's 79-year history.

While Phenix City can't lose again and advance, Rasmus has already put herself in elite LLWS company. She's one strikeout away from breaking Davis' record and may have another chance on the mound thanks to Tuesday's win.

Phenix City will next face Great Lakes winner Hamilton, Ohio, on Wednesday in another elimination game.

articles.title: Wrexham close in on Ekomie and Kabore deals
articles.summary: Manchester City's Issa Kabore is poised to seal a permanent switch to Championship club Wrexham, who are also close to signing left-back Jacques Ekomie from...
articles.body:
Wrexham are poised to sign Issa Kabore on a permanent deal from Manchester City in addition to bringing in left-back Jacques Ekomie from French side Angers .

Burkina Faso international Kabore featured 32 times across all competitions for the Red Dragons in 2025-26.

His eight assists in the Championship were more than any other Wrexham player.

Following seven loan moves away from City, the 25-year-old is now close to sealing a permanent exit from the Etihad Stadium.

The deal for Kabore is worth up to £4.75m - with City having a 20% sell-on clause and matching rights.

Ekomie recently entered the final year of his deal with Angers and reportedly attracted interest from Wrexham's Championship rivals West Ham United and German side Hamburg .

The Red Dragons recruited Liberato Cacace from Italian side Empoli during the 2025 summer transfer window, although the New Zealand international has been plagued by injuries since moving to north Wales.

Ekomie would bolster Phil Parkinson's left-sided options, with the Gabon international and Kabore expected to join full-back Danny Imray, goalkeeper Anthony Patterson and midfielder Ben Whiteman in moving to the Racecourse Ground this summer.

Kabore made a dream start to life with Wrexham last season as he registered a pair of assists on his debut to help the Welsh side earn a 3-2 win over Norwich City at Carrow Road.

He was a mainstay under Parkinson prior to sustaining a hamstring injury while on international duty during the November break.

Kabore made his long-awaited return to action for Burkina Faso in the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations before again featuring prominently for Wrexham in the second half of the season.

The 55-cap international moved to Man City from Mechelen in 2020 before immediately returning to the Belgian club on loan.

He went on to have loan stints with Troyes, Marseille, Luton Town, Benfica and Werder Bremen prior to joining Wrexham on transfer deadline day in September last year.

Right-back Kabore - who operated as a wing-back for Wrexham last term - is poised to leave Man City having failed to make a senior appearance for the club.

Ekomie started his professional career with Bordeaux but secured a switch to top-flight side Angers in the summer of 2024.

He made 21 appearances across all competitions in his debut season for the club, and his impact increased last term.

The 23-year-old featured in all but two of his side's Ligue 1 matches in 2025-26 - with 25 of his 32 appearances in the league being starts.

Prior to his side's 1-1 draw with Watford , Wrexham manager Parkinson stated deals for various players to join the Red Dragons had fallen through in what had been a "difficult window" .

But speaking in his post-match press conference after the Championship contest with the Hornets, the boss said there were "no guarantees" that Wrexham would further bolster their squad prior to the 23:00 BST transfer deadline on 1 September.

Midfielder George Thomason has operated as a makeshift wing-back in the absence of Cacace - who started just eight of Wrexham's 46 league games last season.

Cacace has missed all three of the Red Dragons' matches across all competitions so far this season and still has two years left to run on his contract at the Racecourse Ground.

Wrexham could yet add to their midfield and forward options in the final stages of the summer window.

Parkinson's men return to action against Birmingham City at the Racecourse Ground on Friday night (20:00 BST).

articles.title: Rumour Mongering: Liverpool Move for Ismaïla Sarr After Minteh Failure
articles.summary: Liverpool have gone from struggling to sign Ibrahim Mbaye to struggling to sign Yankuba Minteh. Up next, Ismaïla Sarr.
articles.body:
When you sell Luis Diaz , fail to replace him then spend the entire 2025-26 season struggling due to a lack of pace on the wings, then push Mohamed Salah out of the club because his legs are going and goal involvement numbers have dropped to one every 140 minutes and you no longer see his contract as good value, well, you probably need to sign wingers.

That was the situation for Liverpool and sporting director Richard Hughes at the start of the summer. With a week left in the transfer window and new head coach Andoni Iraola kicking off the season against Newcastle on Sunday with a weaker squad than Arne Slot ended last season with, the Reds still need wingers, plural, along with their so-called Salah replacement.

Which is to say that Liverpool are desperate. And everyone knows it. So. Well done, Richard, good process.

Hughes is struggling to get marquee signing Bradley Barcola across the line, and he's also struggling to get in the second winger the Reds need. On that front, first up was Ibrahim Mbaye . When that stalled out, Yankuba Minteh was the next. When Brighton demanded £80M for him, the question became who might come after that failure. The answer is Ismaïla Sarr.

Or at least that's what the rumour mongers have spit out today . The Crystal Palace winger had been targeted by Galatasaray this summer, but while the Turkish club making a pair of bids they weren't willing to go above €30M (£26M) and Palace were expected to keep him for the coming season.

The chatter has Liverpool coming in offering around double that and willing to pay at least £50M (€58M) to get the deal done. Word from the Palace end is that regardless if they would accept that fee—and it's not entirely clear at the moment if they would—they would still want a replacement lined up before signing off on Sarr's departure, which could be difficult.

In addition to Liverpool being held to ransom by clubs knowing they're desperate, this is another potential problem caused by leaving it late, as for many potential selling clubs even a fee that's over the odds will be less helpful heading into the season than simply keeping the player if there's no time to realistically source a suitable replacement.

As for Sarr, Liverpool have been linked off and on with Sadio Mané 's Senegalese compatriot back to when Mané was still at the club. As such, the right winger is now 28 years old, making him the same age today as Luis Diaz was last summer when Liverpool and sporting director Richard Hughes decided it would be unwise to give the Colombian a lucrative new deal that would have kept him happy at the club.

Hughes then failed to replace Diaz—who then had an outstanding season at Bayern Munich —failed to bring in multiple wing options this summer, and is now at the stage where the club is in such need of correcting his past mistakes that they're willing to spend big on a prime age player with no further upside or resale value.

If there is an upside to signing Sarr, it would be that he's capable of playing across the front line but is most comfortable on the right where Liverpool most need reinforcements. His 21 goals and two assists last season with a goal involvement every 157 minutes is also a solid return.

However, it's a worse return than Diaz had in his final year at the club, it's a worse return than Mohamed Salah had last season, and it's a worse return than Cody Gakpo has had for Liverpool up until last season. All of which is to say Liverpool would be stronger today if Richard Hughes had just done nothing and kept Diaz and Salah than they will be if he now manages to sign Sarr.

Well done, Richard. Good fucking process.

articles.title: Eagles blank Falcons for first win of season in county boys soccer match
articles.summary: HARPERSFIELD — Coaches David Bell and Jamie Lee both said the Jefferson and Geneva boys soccer teams, respectively, have been working on a lot of different t...
articles.body:
HARPERSFIELD — Coaches David Bell and Jamie Lee both said the Jefferson and Geneva boys soccer teams, respectively, have been working on a lot of different things in the early going of the 2026 season.

On Tuesday night though, Lee's Eagles earned a 2-0 victory at SPIRE Academy.

The game was decided by a couple of kicks in the net, but Geneva's defense was the most influential factor.

"It's something we've been working hard on this year," Lee said of the defensive effort. "I didn't think we did as well as we should have, but we still came away with the win, so we're very happy with that because the boys needed a confidence boost."

Geneva earned its first win the after starting the season with losses to West Geauga 4-1 and Harvey 4-2.

Against the Falcons, the Eagles' midfielders were able to keep the ball in their offensive end and limit Jefferson's opportunities to mount any attacks.

"We are trying to work more on passing and not dribbling so much, so controlling the midfield is something we've been working on, and we did do that well [Tuesday night]," Lee said.

Drew Clutter put the Eagles on the board by taking a perfectly placed pass from Tanner Williams right in front of the goal box and sending it into the net for a 1-0 lead with 13 minutes remaining in the first half.

The score stayed 1-0, until the Eagles received an insurance goal on a header by Zach McKinney off a corner kick in the second half.

But the bigger story was the Eagles defense that kept the frustrated Jefferson all night.

"They had a big defender who slid the mid sometimes, it was really hard to get past him," Bell said. "It was our best player against their best player, and they got the better of it [Tuesday night]."

Geneva outshot the Falcons by a count of 13-3.

Jefferson goalie Gabe Wiliams had eight saves, while Geneva's Randy Doll posted two.

The Falcons, who went winless a year ago, sustained their first loss of the season.

They opened with wins over Brookfield 7-0 and Brooklyn 2-1.

Bell said he believes his team can be much more competitive this fall.

He said the Falcons are still young, but the players who were pushed into starting roles a year ago are all back with a year of experience.

"My expectations this year is to try and go .500," the coach said. "With the schedule we play, I think we can get eight or nine wins. We have nine starters back from last year, six of them were starting as freshmen, and three of them sophomores."

Geneva will be at home against Perry Thursday night.
authors: Mike Shaffer, Star Beacon, Ashtabula, Ohio

articles.title: Calvin Austin injury: Giants’ WR done for season with torn ACL
articles.summary: NY Giants receiver Calvin Austin is officially done for the season.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Calvin Austin III tore his ACL, per a report from Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team .

Austin tore his ACL in a non-contact injury suffered in practice on Tuesday.

The injury is a definite blow to the Giants offense, speedy slot receiver had been having a great camp. Austin quickly developed a rapport with QB Jaxson Dart and emerged as one of Dart's favorite targets in practice. He was also emerging as one of the Giants' most explosive options, with his 4.3 speed and agility giving opposing defenders fits.

Austin was signed away from the Pittsburgh Steelers on a one-year, $1.5 million contract and looked like he might far out-play his deal.

Now his season is over before it even begins and the Giants will have to figure out a new plan for the slot receiver, and find another source of explosiveness for their offense.

articles.title: Colts edge rushers named position group to watch for potential trades
articles.summary: CBS Sports identified the Colts’ packed edge rusher room as one teams could monitor for potential trades or waiver claims before final cuts.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts' depth at defensive end could make the position worth watching as the NFL's roster deadline approaches.

CBS Sports' Josh Edwards included the Colts ' edge rushers in the company of position groups around the league that could produce trade or waiver-wire targets before teams trim their rosters to 53 players.

Indianapolis has Laiatu Latu and Arden Key atop its current depth chart, with Jaylahn Tuimoloau, Micheal Clemons , George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry also competing for spots.

"They could, in theory, keep six edge rushers," Edwards wrote, adding that the decision could depend on roster numbers elsewhere and special teams value.

The cramped room follows an offseason in which the Colts signed Key and Clemons after Kwity Paye departed. Indianapolis has also invested heavily in young pass rushers, using a first-round pick on Latu in 2024, a second-rounder on Tuimoloau in 2025 and selections on Gumbs and Curry in the 2026 draft.

The rookies have provided nice returns so far. Curry recorded five tackles, a sack, two quarterback hits, two tackles for loss and two passes defensed in the preseason opener against the New England Patriots, while Gumbs also recorded a sack.

Indianapolis may laud that flexibility, but it could also attract calls from teams looking for help before final cuts.

articles.title: What you need to know about Nashville Predators, ViewLift streaming agreement
articles.summary: The Nashville Predators will partner with ViewLift, a product under the sports platform DAZN, for their direct-to-consumer streaming platform.
articles.body:
The Nashville Predators have announced more details about their upcoming direct-to-consumer streaming service ahead of the 2026-27 season.

On Aug. 26, the Predators unveiled a multi-year agreement with ViewLift, a streaming product recently acquired by sports entertainment platform DAZN. ViewLift will carry all non-nationally televised Predators games starting this season.

ViewLift will give Predators fans direct access to live games, on-demand replays, highlights, and original programming. It will be available on the web, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku TV, Fire TV, and Android TV.

Pricing and streaming plans for this new service will be announced at a later date. The service should be available to anyone in the Predators' regional viewing area, which includes Tennessee, Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi and Georgia.

The Predators are one of 18 professional sports franchises in the U.S. that will be carried on ViewLift.

This is the latest development in the Predators' new broadcast rights era under Scripps Sports. On April 7, the team announced a multi-year broadcast deal with Scripps, which owns NewsChannel 5 in the Nashville area. Starting this season, all non-nationally televised Predators games will appear on WNPX (Channel 28) a channel called "The Spot." According to their website , the channel is also available on cable and satellite services like DirectTV and Xfinity.

articles.title: NHL legend Wayne Gretzky remembers icons Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau on Hockey Hall of Fame induction anniversary
articles.summary: NHL News: On the anniversary of Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau's Hockey Hall of Fame induction, Wayne Gretzky celebrates their legacy and impact on the NHL, highlighting their achievements on and off the ice.
articles.body: Wayne Gretzky honours Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau on the anniversary of their Hockey Hall of Fame induction, celebrating the legacy of two NHL legends. The tribute was held Aug. 24, the anniversary of the day the two legendary players were inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1972.Widely regarded as one of the best to ever play in the NHL, Gretzky praised Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau not only for what they did on the ice, but also for the reputation they built off of it. His comments served as another reminder of the impact the two players continue to have on the pro game.Wayne Gretzky honors Gordie Howe and Jean BeliveauWayne Gretzky has paid tribute to Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau, calling the NHL legends two of the classiest athletes ever.Howe and Beliveau were enshrined in the Hockey Hall of Fame on Aug. 24, 1972, after careers that made them defining figures of their generation.The two players were also given an unusual honour when the Hall of Fame waived its traditional three-year waiting period. It was an indication of the remarkable stature they had already attained in the professional hockey world.Howe spent the bulk of his storied NHL career with the Detroit Red Wings, becoming synonymous with the franchise and earning the nickname “Mr Hockey.” In his career, he won four Stanley Cups and six Hart Trophies.At the same time, Beliveau was becoming one of the great stars of the Montreal Canadiens. The center won 10 Stanley Cup titles with Montreal and earned the Hart Trophy twice in his Hall of Fame career.What made Gordie Howe and Jean Beliveau NHL iconsHowe's career was marked by extraordinary longevity, physical toughness and production. He played 26 NHL seasons and was a major figure in professional hockey long after the era in which he first became a star.Beliveau combined size, skill and leadership to emerge as a leading figure on the Montreal Canadiens championship teams. His achievements helped make him one of the most celebrated players in franchise history.Their legacies went beyond the statistics. Both players were respected ambassadors of the game and known for their professionalism and conduct.When Wayne Gretzky reflected on their NHL legacyGretzky’s tribute was a chance to revisit the historic induction of Howe and Beliveau on the anniversary. His recognition also crossed generations of NHL greatness.The anniversary is more than just about the 1972 ceremony. Howe and Beliveau helped shape the history of the league, and Gretzky was one of the players who helped change the profile of the sport in the world.Their careers are still part of the broader NHL record book, ensuring that the two legends will remain prominently featured in discussions about hockey’s greatest players.Gretzky’s recognition of Howe and Beliveau also signals the respect between generations of NHL stars. articles.title: What is F1 star Max Verstappen’s Max vs 100 event about? When and where to watch the unique racing event?
articles.summary: International Sports News: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen is set for a very different racing challenge. The Red Bull star will take on 100 drivers in a unique.
articles.body: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen is set for a very different racing challenge. The Red Bull star will take on 100 drivers in a unique go-kart race at Silverstone on September 16. Verstappen will start at the back of the 101-driver field and try to overtake every competitor.The event, called Max vs 100, will be broadcast live on Disney+ and ESPN. The race will feature athletes, streamers, content creators and fans from around the world. A purpose-built circuit has been created at Silverstone for the unusual event.What is Max Verstappen’s Max vs 100 event?Max vs 100 is a special go-karting event designed around one simple idea. Max Verstappen will have to fight his way through a field of 100 drivers. Unlike a normal race, the Dutchman will not start from the front. He will begin in 101st place.His challenge will be to pass all 100 drivers and reach the front. The event will take place at Silverstone, the famous home of the British Grand Prix. A new circuit has been built specifically for the huge field.The track was designed by former racing driver and karting world champion David Terrien. He has created the layout to handle 101 karts at the same time.The event will take Verstappen back to where his racing journey began. The Red Bull driver first drove a go-kart when he was just four years old. By the age of seven, he was competing in championships.Karting played a major role in developing his racing skills. Verstappen learned how to start races, defend positions and make overtaking moves.Verstappen is excited about returning to karting.“In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking. Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it’s always nice to return. It’s about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I’ve done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things”, Verstappen said.However, Verstappen knows the race will be chaotic.When asked what he was most looking forward to, the four-time champion gave a simple answer.Who will race Max Verstappen?The 100-driver field will include competitors from different sports and areas of entertainment.Ultrarunner Arda Saatçi will take part. Basketball shooting specialist Chris “Lethal Shooter” Matthews is also set to race. Freestyle mountain biker Matt Jones will be among the drivers as well. Popular streamers TheGrefg, Caedrel and TheDonato will also get behind the wheel.The rest of the field will include content creators, personalities and everyday fans from around the world. The complete list of 100 drivers will be confirmed before race day.When and where to watch Max Verstappen’s Max vs 100 event?Max vs 100 will take place on September 16 at Silverstone.There will be no spectators at the venue.
