articles.title: Renault actualiza el 5 eléctrico y le permite jugar a ser un Clio Williams
articles.standfirst: Además de ese look tan especial, ofrece mayor autonomía, una versión básica muy mejorada y hasta la IA de Gemini
articles.summary: Además de ese look tan especial, ofrece mayor autonomía, una versión básica muy mejorada y hasta la IA de Gemini
articles.body: El renacido Renault 5 no lleva demasiado tiempo entre nosotros (apenas dos años), pero la marca francesa ya va a introducir mejoras interesantes a partir de este final de verano en su carismático urbano eléctrico. Su vuelta a la vida ha sido todo un éxito. En Europa está en el top 5 de modelos más vendidos con propulsión eléctrica en este 2026, mientas que en España está en el top 7 hasta julio. Pero la competencia aprieta y crece y Renault quiere estar preparado para ello. Una de las principales mejoras llega en un apartado que van a agradecer sus compradores: la autonomía de la batería. Aunque las pilas no cambian (se sigue ofreciendo con capacidades de 40 y 52 kWh), el alcance es mayor: ahora se va a 315 y 430 km respectivamente. Es una mejora muy pequeña, casi testimonial respecto al modelo original, que homologaba 312 y 410 km. ¿Cómo se ha conseguido? En base a mejoras en el software de las baterías (algo que ya hemos visto en modelos más veteranos de otros fabricantes) y con retoques aerodinámicos, como los nuevos retrovisores y bajos. Habrá más opciones para personalizar su look (uno de los puntos fuertes de este modelo) y nuevos elementos prácticos como un cargador inalámbrico para móvil refrigerado y más potente, un programa de conducción Smart (que sustitye al Individual) que selecciona el más adecuado en cada momento según las necesidades de conducción, y la IA de Google, Gemini, también se incorpora al sistema multimedia. Además, hay otro cambio, en este caso en la versión de acceso s la gama Renault 5. Aunque en España no se ha comercializado, había una versión de 95 CV, criticada en su día porque no permitía carga rápida, que ahora se mejora sustancialmente... precisamente modificando este aspecto (quién sabe si ahora la veremos en España). El nuevo Renault 5 básico heredará el motor del Twingo con 110 caballos de potencia (hasta ahora se ofrecía con 122 y 150) y una batería LFP ligeramente más pequeña, con 36,4 kWh (en lugar de 40) para un alcance de 305 km (siempre por encima de la barrera psicológica de los 300 kilómetros homologados). Una versión que le permitirá medirse en precio con la competencia china (BYD Dolphin Surf) y europea (Volkswagen ID.Polo). Buceando entre sus nuevas posibilidades encontramos una combinación de colores con un especial significado en Renault. De hecho, la marca del rombo ofrece entre sus imágenes de prensa una configuración de su Renault 5 que no es casual: con llantas doradas y un color azul con reminiscencias pasadas. Se trata de un homenaje al Renault Clio Williams (recordemos que el Clio fue el modelo que dio el relevo al R5 original). articles.title: WWE Rumors on OTM's Backstage Reaction, Blake Monroe's Debut and New Tag Team on SmackDown
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reported Internal Reception for OTM's Main Roster Call-Up

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

OTM made a shocking debut on WWE's main roster during Monday night's episode of Raw, as they showed up alongside Royce Keys and interrupted the main event pitting The Usos against LA Knight and Solo Sikoa.

According to False Finish , the backstage reaction to Bronco Nima and Lucien Price debuting on Raw was "very positive" within WWE.

It was also reported by False Finish that WWE had been planning to put OTM in a stable with Keys "for a few weeks."

Nima and Price signed with WWE in 2022 and began teaming up almost immediately. Although they gained some momentum as a team in NXT, they never managed to capture the NXT Tag Team Championships.

It felt like OTM had more left to accomplish in NXT, which is why it came as such a big surprise when they made their presence felt on Raw.

Nima had recently been pulling double duty on both NXT and AAA, as he was part of the Perros del Mal stable in AAA since June.

However, Nima was kicked out of Perros del Mal last week in a move that apparently set the stage for him and Price to move up to WWE's main roster.

Keys has a ton of unfinished business with The Bloodline after Jacob Fatu put him out of commission, and with OTM now by his side, he seems poised to wreak havoc over the red brand.

WWE's Reported In-Ring Debut Plan for Monroe

Blake Monroe's scheduled WWE main roster debut match against Giulia on SmackDown last week never actually got started, but a match between them reportedly could still be in the cards.

According to False Finish , WWE decision-makers have discussed adding Monroe vs. Giulia to the Sunday Night's Main Event card on Sept. 6.

While the match is being considered, False Finish added that nothing is official yet regarding Monroe vs. Giulia being part of SNME.

Following her run in NXT, which saw her hold the Women's North American Championship once, Monroe's impending arrival on SmackDown was announced back in April.

Vignettes were shown for weeks on end, and she took part in a number of backstage segments, but WWE continually held off on booking Monroe in her first main roster match.

It seemed as though that was finally going to change last week on SmackDown when Monroe vs. Giulia was advertised for the show, but the bell never rang for the match, as The Glamour attacked Giulia beforehand.

Since WWE has waited this long for Monroe to have a match and is now building a story between her and Giulia, it makes sense for Blake to finally have her debut bout on a show bigger than an episode of SmackDown.

Sunday Night's Main Event undoubtedly qualifies, and there is room on the card with only three matches announced for SNME as of this week.

Reported Tag Team Name for Nakamura, Kyoki

WWE reportedly has a name picked out for the new tag team comprised for Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki.

According to False Finish , Nakamura and Kyoki are expected to be known collectively as Bakusai, which is a Japanese word that translates into "explosion" in English.

Mike Reichlin of SEScoops.com reported in June that WWE had filed to trademark the name "Bakusai," and many assumed at the time that it would be the name for the incoming Hiromu Takahashi.

However, after weeks of teasing his new ally, Nakamura revealed Takahashi under the name Kyoki.

As for the Bakusai tag team name, it draws from Kyoki's past, as he was known by the nickname "The Ticking Time Bomb" during his New Japan Pro-Wrestling tenure.

In recent weeks, Nakamura and Kyoki have made it clear that the WWE Tag Team Championships are on their radar, which suggests that a rivalry between Bakusai and The MFTs is on the horizon.

articles.title: Ismaila Sarr transfer news: Liverpool make approach for Senegal forward after stalled talks for Yankuba Minteh
articles.summary: Liverpool are considering their options after talks have stalled with Brighton over a deal to sign Yankuba Minteh; Sarr missed Palace's opening weekend defeat at Everton. Reports claimed he was refusing to train, but it is understood that the winger is currently injured
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola's side are considering their options after talks stalled with Brighton over Yankuba Minteh.

Sarr is one of the players Liverpool are exploring as they look to reinforce out wide.

Palace have no intention of letting Sarr go at this stage and consider the 28-year-old to be not for sale. He has three years left on his contract.

Sarr missed Palace's opening weekend defeat at Everton. Reports claimed he was refusing to train but it is understood that the winger is currently injured.

Asked about Sarr's future during his press conference on Wednesday, Palace boss Pierre Sage said: "I understand for everybody that to have this kind of contact is difficult because you hesitate a lot, but for the moment he is with us.

"He is under contract, he is injured, and maybe you can link his injury and the situation.

"But for me, he is honest, and I have no problem with that. I spoke with him this morning about that. Yesterday about that too, and we just want him on the pitch, and all the rest for the other people"

PSG's Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's main target but there is a possibility that Liverpool sign more than one winger.

Cody Gakpo is the subject of interest from Tottenham and Manchester City. Liverpool are not open to selling the Dutchman as things stand and would need two wingers to be signed if he did depart.

Liverpool's talks with Brighton for Minteh are not progressing as things stand.

Brighton are holding out for £80m after rejecting two bids from Liverpool. The latest offer from Andoni Iraola's side was worth £60m.

Liverpool are currently unwilling to reach that figure for Minteh, who is injured and expected to be out until October.

The Pittsburgh Steelers aren't finished making roster moves as their preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills draws ever closer.

On Tuesday, the Steelers announced the signing of safety Brandon Hill . In a related move, the team released wide receiver Joaquin Davis.

Hill, who played college football at Pittsburgh (2019-2022), was drafted by the Houston Texans in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft. Hill was waived by the Texans in March 2025 due to a failed physical but re-signed with their practice squad, only to be released one week later.

articles.title: Same but different: How Freedom 250 and Detroit Grand Prix compare.
articles.summary: Backdrops aside, the Freedom 250 GP and Detroit GP are very alike. How Penske Entertainment puts on an urban circus in two great U.S. cities.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. ― The NTT IndyCar Freedom 250 race around the National mall was one of the most electric races in the history of American motorsport. Like the Indianapolis 500 on Memorial Day weekend, it was a stage unlike any other ― its trophy coveted by drivers and teams.

In execution, however, D.C.'s street race celebrating the nation's 250th birthday was similar to Penske Entertainment's annual home race, the Detroit Grand Prix.

The traveling IndyCar circus is the world's most challenging race series because it tests drivers (and organizers) on venues from 240-mph ovals to writhing road courses to gritty street courses. This year, IndyCar had five urban slugfests on its 18-race calendar: St. Petersburg, Florida; Long Beach, California; Markham, Ontario; Detroit and D.C.

The latter pair have the most in common. "The track is a lot like Detroit, actually," said Indy 500 winner and Andretti Global ace Marcus Ericsson in a trackside D.C. interview. "Very bumpy with a long front straight that is the best spot to pass."

A comparison of the unlikely fraternal twins:

Both the Freedom 250 and Detroit GP are very aware of their optics. Detroit is built around the Renaissance Center, one of the most imposing, recognizable skyscrapers in North America.

The Freedom 250 layout was originally supposed to take place on Capitol Hill between the Capitol nuilding and the Supreme Court on 1 st Street. Politics nixed that and organizers settled for the National Mall. The backdrop was still extraordinary:

Pits off Pennsylvania Avenue main straightaway in front of the National Gallery of Art

Turns 2 and 3 splitting the National Archives and the Department of Justice. Back straight on Independence Avenue in the shadow of the Air & Space Museum's three monolithic facades.

"Jumping into the car on pit lane and looking down at the Capitol, its spectacular," said Ericsson. "Super cool, and for our sport a ginormous opportunity for us to reach new fans."

Running 'round RenCen means the Detroit GP has to keep an international border crossing open. For three days, vehicles continue to cross between the United States and Canada via the Detroit-Windsor Tunned. Emerge from Canada and head east on Jefferson Avenue going 35 mph. In the westbound lanes? IndyCars doing 180.

Washington's patchwork of federal land, city streets and historic buildings meant that Penske Entertainment had to get a staggering 1,350 permits approved.

Both circuits are 1.7 miles long. On gridded streets with 90-degree turns and little elevation change. Detroit requires sealing 162 manhole covers (lest IndyCars' aerodynamics suck them out of the ground). The D.C. track? 200 covers were secured. Chip Ganassi Racing star Alex Palou won pole in Detroit this summer with a lap time of 1.01.9 minutes (96 mph average speed). Palou won pole in D.C. with a lap time of 56.9 seconds (108 mph average). Detroit top speed is 180 mph, D.C. 170.

That's expected in Detroit, given our brutal freeze-thaw seasons. But Washington's moderate climate promised smoother thoroughfares like St Petersburg or Long Beach. Didn't happen. Especially difficult were bumps into Turn 6 on Independence Avenue at 140 mph and Turn 2 at the end of Pennsylvania Avenue at 170 mph. As Ericsson predicted, the latter was the best place to pass if you could brave the bump.

"You get a concussion every lap," complained driver Louis Foster after qualifying.

Detroit has a reputation as a dysfunctional town, but it's a piker compared with D.C. Like Detroit mayors, D.C.'s Muriel Bowser embraced a race estimated to bring the region over $100 million in spending from 150,000 visitors and flush sponsors. Still, both events ran into local conservationist opposition. Penske moved downtown from Belle Isle in 2023 in part due to activists protesting use of the bucolic park. In D.C., a group called the Living New Deal protested that vibrations from screaming IndyCars would damage art.

But D.C. has another layer of politics: Congress v. White House.

Advertising is prohibited on Capitol Hill, and Senate Democrats refused to give IndyCar a waiver for their sponsor-wrapped cars. Despite over 80 trips to the Hill by Penske President Bud Denker and his team, the GP hit a roadblock until President Donald Trump signed an executive order in January moving the race to the Mall.

The politics even sucked in drivers, a rare feat in motorsports.

"While you struggle with the cost of gas, Trump offers you the spectacle of an IndyCar race hoping you will not notice," Sen. Adam Schiff, D-California, complained Sunday, August 23 on Twitter. "More taxpayer money spent on his self-aggrandizing distractions. And you get higher taxes and higher costs."

IndyCar driver Graham Rahal responded: "No, no, Adam. He wanted you to notice and bask in the pride of being AMERICAN, watch great racing and patriotism on display. Not only that, this was privately funded, not government although it drove thousands of folks to the DC area that have never been (that's economic impact for you)."

Over three days, the 2026 Detroit race drew 156,000 fans to downtown Detroit. The Freedom 250 stuffed 150,000 fans into the National Mall over two days. General admission tickets were free, as they are for Friday Frix Prix in Detroit.

The Detroit GP gets a flyover from Air Force F-16s. The Freedom 250 featured F-22 fighters, B1/B2/B-52 bombers and Air Force One.

The bumpy track and close concrete barriers meant six caution periods over the Freedom GP's 250 miles. Detroit had six cautions over 165 miles.

Honda-powered IndyCars have spoiled sponsor Chevrolet's home Grand Prix all four years it's been held downtown. Honda power won the inaugural Freedom 250 too. Engineers credit Honda engines' superior fuel efficiency, which gives them a leg up on thirsty street circuits (Honda teams have won all five street races this year).

Then again, only Honda has Kyle Kirkwood, considered the series' best street racer. He won Detroit in 2025 and D.C. this year.

Henry Payne is auto critic for The Detroit News. Find him at hpayne@detroitnews.com or @HenryEPayne.

articles.title: After ouster of GM Dana Brown, Astros owner Jim Crane says manager Joe Espada will finish season
articles.summary: A day after parting ways with general manager Dana Brown, Houston Astros owner Jim Crane addressed the move and said manager Joe Espada will remain in the ro...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — A day after parting ways with general manager Dana Brown, Houston Astros owner Jim Crane addressed the move and said manager Joe Espada will remain in the role for the remainder of the season.

Before opening a three-game series against the Yankees , the Astros moved on from Brown, whose contract was set to expire at the end of the season. The team described the decision as mutual. Houston announced senior adviser Jeff Bagwell and assistant general managers Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff will take over Brown's responsibilities, while Crane will oversee baseball operations during the transition.

"There's no good time for any of that, you know, when you let someone go," Crane said outside the Houston clubhouse. "Just out of respect for Dana, we thought that was a time that would give him a little space to regroup. He's a great talent. He's been in the business a long time to get settled and to get back to work somewhere else."

Brown was hired in January 2023 and succeeded James Click, who was fired six days after Houston won its second World Series title.

"We worked together very closely for three and a half years," Espada said. "He gave me the opportunity to be manager of this team. It was tough. It was a tough conversation, but he was grateful for the opportunity and I'm grateful for our relationship and how we grind through this together, but it was emotional. It was a lot of emotions behind our conversation."

Brown helped the Astros reach a seventh straight ALCS, which they lost in seven games to the Texas Rangers . Houston lost in a wild-card series to Detroit in 2024 and last season missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016 when it finished three games behind Seattle in the AL West and lost a tiebreaker with the Tigers for final wild-card spot.

"Not everybody's been able to do it, that's a good run," Crane said. "We hope to keep that going. We had a little hiccup last year where we didn't make the playoffs but we're right there. I think some few adjustments we can get back to that and some good decisions. Certainly you got to keep working on it but the expectation that I have is that we're in the playoffs every year. It's hard to win every year, but to get there."

The Astros began this year 20-31 but were only 5 1/2 games out of first place in a weak AL West on May 20. Houston (65-66) recovered to win 40 of its next 66 games through a 6-3 win over San Diego on Aug. 7 but entered Tuesday with nine losses in 14 games, including four to the Angels and A's, though Crane said that performance did not influence his decision to dismiss Brown.

"That didn't have anything to do with it," Crane said. "We're focused on winning the AL, winning the division and that's our focus but that didn't have anything to do with it."

Espada was promoted from bench coach after the 2023 season when Dusty Baker retired. He helped the Astros recover from a 12-24 start to win their seventh AL West crown in eight seasons in 2024 and began Tuesday with a 240-214 record.

"I don't know where that got mixed up, but that's the same answer I gave since the first of the year," Crane said. "We told him we'd deal with that at the end of the season and we've never changed that answer all year long."

Before Crane addressed reporters for nearly 10 minutes, he met with Espada.

"Focus on winning today, that's how I left that," Espada said. "My responsibility is to lead this team. We have a very important stretch of games here. So I walk out of our office ready to go."

articles.title: Warriors Sign Ex-Celtics Forward to Help Stephen Curry
articles.summary: The Massachusetts native never played a game for the Celtics.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have a new shooter on their roster.

ESPN's Shams Charania broke the news that Georges Niang has agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Warriors.

Niang, 33, is a career 39.9 percent 3-point shooter who will help space the floor for Stephen Curry .

A Massachusetts native, Niang never appeared in a game for the Boston Celtics , but he was a part of the franchise for around a month. On July 7, 2025, the Atlanta Hawks sent him to Boston as part of the Kristaps Porzingis trade. The Celtics then traded Niang to the Utah Jazz on August 6, 2025.

Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens said at the time that he would've "loved" Niang to play for the Celtics. The decision to part ways with him was ultimately a financial one .

"Obviously being from here you want to play for your hometown team, but I don't think as a professional athlete you have enough time to be heartbroken or upset," Niang said . "You just move on and go along. It's just another part of the journey."

Niang will now get an opportunity to carve out a role in Steve Kerr's rotation.

Niang missed all of last season due to a foot injury. In 2024-25, he averaged 9.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists while shooting 40.6 percent from 3.

Over two-thirds of Niang's shot attempts in his career have come from 3-point range. He gives the Warriors a reliable frontcourt shooter who can open up the floor for Curry, Jimmy Butler and Draymond Green .

In addition to Niang, the Warriors agreed to a one-year deal with Brandon Williams.

The two signings complete Golden State's 15-man roster.

articles.title: First look at Kayshon Boutte in Texans uniform with new jersey number
articles.summary: Kayshon Boutte appeared on the practice field with the Texans for the first time wearing a new jersey number.
articles.body:
Former New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte appeared on the practice field with the Houston Texans for the first time on Wednesday, and he was wearing a new jersey number.

After spending the last three years wearing No. 9 in New England , Boutte will don No. 88 in Houston.

The former sixth-round draft pick stole headlines on Monday after he was traded to the Texans for a 2028 seventh-round draft pick and second-year safety Jaylen Reed . Patriots fans weren't too happy about the return on the trade being a late-round pick nearly two years away and a player who contributed mostly on special teams for the Texans last season.

There was hope that the Patriots would keep Boutte, along with the other six receivers currently viewed as locks to make the 53-man roster, including A.J. Brown , Romeo Doubs , DeMario Douglas , Mack Hollins , Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III .

Boutte has joined a Texans team with more questions than answers at receiver.

Outside of Nico Collins , Jayden Higgins was expected to be the other big-bodied receiving target, but he suffered a season-ending injury. The team is likely curious to see if Boutte can help fill that void as a legitimate No. 2 option. With that said, there are no guarantees that he will even start for the Texans.

"Just talking to people in Houston, it doesn't sound like he's assumed to be a starter even there," NBC Sports Boston's Phil Perry said on Boutte, when appearing on Toucher & Hardy . "…They're not necessarily like enamored with this guy. They don't feel as if they've gotten one over the Patriots and this is like this massive steal for them, even though they have a need at the position now, given that they've dealt with some injuries there recently."

articles.title: Registration opens for 2026 YMCA of Greater Pittsburgh Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary: Registration opened Wednesday for the 36th Annual YMCA of Greater Pittsburgh Turkey Trot presented by UPMC Health Plan, scheduled for Thanksgiving Day, Nov....
articles.body:
Registration opened Wednesday for the 36th Annual YMCA of Greater Pittsburgh Turkey Trot presented by UPMC Health Plan, scheduled for Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26.

Organizers expect more than 8,500 runners and walkers to participate in the annual holiday event.

Proceeds from the event benefit YMCA food pantry programs and the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank. The initiative provides food assistance and community resources to residents facing food insecurity across the region.

"The Turkey Trot is proof of what happens when a community comes together with a shared purpose," said Amy Kienle, president and CEO of the YMCA of Greater Pittsburgh. "At the Y, we believe we are for all—and on Thanksgiving morning, you can see that belief come to life as people of all ages, backgrounds and abilities come together to move, celebrate and give back."

Race options for the event include a 5-mile, 5K, 1-mile and the Double Gobble challenge, which combines the 5-mile and 5K courses. Double Gobble participants who complete both races will receive a special gift.

A virtual registration option is also available for those unable to attend in person. All participants will receive a long-sleeve shirt and, for the first time this year, a finisher medal upon crossing the finish line. Click here for more information.

Organizers are offering half-price registration for participants ages 5 to 18, while children age 4 and under can enter for free. The expanded offerings follow last year's event, which drew more than 8,000 participants from 38 states and six countries.

"The Turkey Trot has become a beloved Pittsburgh Thanksgiving tradition because it brings people together for a great cause," said Bob Shooer, interim CEO and board president of P3R, the organization producing the event. "Whether you're running, walking or cheering from the sidelines, it's a fun way to start the holiday with family and friends while also giving back to our community."

articles.summary: David Gabriel Georges has burst onto the national scene as one of the nation’s premier prospects in the 2027 recruiting class. After a standout performance e...
articles.body:
David Gabriel Georges has burst onto the national scene as one of the nation's premier prospects in the 2027 recruiting class. After a standout performance earlier this month on national TV, he drew plenty of attention from across the college sports world.

And he apparently caught the attention of Texas quarterback Arch Manning, whose younger cousin Marshall Manning is teammates with DGG at Baylor School (Tenn.). The elder Manning was asked about Marshall on Wednesday, but made sure to shout out the five-star Tennessee running back commit as well.

"He's at a really good school," Arch Manning said. "They have a really good running back; he looks yoked. What are they feeding those guys?"

articles.title: Giants reveal significant Willy Adames injury news amid Reds series
articles.summary: The Giants placed Adames on the injured list on Monday.
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants may have to make do without their starting shortstop.

Willy Adames was placed on the injured list on Monday by the NL West club.

According to Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle , Adames has been diagnosed with a sprained ulnar collateral ligament in his left elbow.

"It's his non-throwing (left) elbow, so it's possible that rest and rehab will be all that's required," Slusser wrote.

Reportedly, Adames suffered the injury while sliding into home plate on Sunday against the Boston Red Sox .

He slid feet first and scored from second base on an RBI single, but it was an awkward slide. It appeared Adames had to stop himself from falling using his left arm.

"It's something that I think he can work to rehab, see where it's at, get it reevaluated, and then go from there," Giants manager Tony Vitello told Slusser about Adames' injury.

This is the second year of the seven-year, $182 million contract Adames signed with the Giants before the 2025 season.

Like many Giants players, he's having a down year at the plate. In 121 games, Adames is hitting .230/.289/.424 with 21 home runs and a .713 OPS, 43 points below his career average.

articles.title: Arch Manning’s on-field antics exposed as one teammate reveals Texas QB’s ‘annoying’ habit
articles.summary: Arch Manning’s competitive side takes center stage as Texas LB Justin Cryer reveals how the QB gets inside defenders’ heads during games.
articles.body:
Arch Manning has already established himself as one of the most recognizable quarterbacks in college football. After a breakout first full season as Texas ' starter, Manning enters the 2026 campaign with expectations extending far beyond Austin.

With his talent, family name and growing reputation, the spotlight surrounding Manning quarterback shows no signs of fading. While much of the attention surrounding him has focused on his performances on the field, Texas linebacker Justin Cryer offered an interesting glimpse into another side of the quarterback on Tuesday.

According to Cryer, Manning has developed a habit of making a play and then coming up behind a defensive player to deliver a quick chirp that only the player can hear. It is seemingly part of Manning's approach to the mental side of the game, using small exchanges to keep defenders thinking about him even after the play is over.

The comments provide an entertaining look at Manning's personality and suggest that his competitive edge goes beyond simply making plays with his arm and legs.

Manning entered the 2025 season surrounded by considerable Heisman Trophy hype and expectations. Although he struggled at times early in the campaign, he gradually found his rhythm and displayed the explosive playmaking ability that made him one of the most highly anticipated quarterbacks in the country.

Manning entered last season with Heisman hype but struggled initially. However, he showed his splash later.

Across 13 starts in 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also made a significant impact as a runner, rushing for 399 yards and a team-high 10 touchdowns.

Manning's strongest moments came when Texas needed them most, particularly during the postseason. In the Citrus Bowl against Michigan , he recorded 376 total yards and four touchdowns as Texas secured a 41-27 victory. He passed for 221 yards and two touchdowns while adding a career-high 155 rushing yards and two more scores on the ground.

If Manning can build on that late-season momentum, improve his efficiency and continue limiting turnovers, he could put himself in the middle of the Heisman conversation once again while potentially leading Texas on another deep College Football Playoff run.

articles.title: British sprinter Matthew Brennan continues dream Vuelta a Espana debut with stage five win
articles.summary: The 21-year-old from Darlington, competing in his first grand tour, was a clear winner on stage five
articles.body:
British starlet Matthew Brennan continued a brilliant start to his first grand tour as he took a dominant victory on stage five of the Vuelta a Espana .

The 21-year-old arrived at the race in sparkling form after two stage wins at the Vuelta a Burgos earlier this month and he immediately made himself at home at grand tour level, winning stage two's chaotic finish in Manosque, before doubling up just three days later.

His Visma-Lease a Bike squad delivered the perfect leadout in Roquetes, Terres de l'Ebre, with Wout van Aert and Christophe Laporte launching him into the final 150m and the Briton holding off his rivals with ease, holding up two fingers in celebration as he crossed the line.

Brennan said: "It's better than a normal day job! It's fantastic, second one in the bag, first grand tour. You can see throughout the day everyone just went full [gas], I'm very thankful to finish it off again, I think the boys are also quite relieved.

"[The leadout] was pretty spot on, we had the two boys pulling on the front until the final few k, then Wout and Christophe, the best guys you can have for this type of thing. They supported me until the final. Last corner I lost my wheel a bit, the paint was a bit slippery, but glad we could finish with the arms in the air.

"I wouldn't say I'm a sprinter, I can climb a little bit. Especially with the support I have here, when you've got these guys with you it really gives you the confidence to go on and achieve more."

Regardless of his own self-classification Brennan has proved a force to be reckoned with on either classic, flat sprinters' terrain or more punchy sprint finishes. Perhaps the most appropriate characterisation for him would be as an all-around Classics rider in the same vein as Van Aert.

Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe's pure sprinter Jordi Meeus - who most notably won on the Champs-Elysees in 2023 - was second with EF Education-EasyPost's Vincenzo Albanese third, and Laporte held on for seventh after his leadout.

Race leader Tadej Pogacar 's UAE Team Emirates-XRG squad controlled proceedings until the latter stages, prompting speculation the Slovenian might fancy a go at a third stage win of this race already.

But ultimately the sprinters' teams took over to set up a rare bunch finish in a Vuelta with minimal chances for the fast men.

A category-three climb, the 3.9km Puerto de Pauls, inside the final 30km eliminated some of the sprinters, including Lidl-Trek's Mads Pedersen, but Brennan was well protected within the peloton and appeared barely troubled by his efforts in the finale.

Pogacar remains in the overall lead after the 173.3km run from Falset, Costa Daurada, with no change in the general classification. His compatriot Primoz Roglic of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe sits 3'21" off his lead, with Enric Mas of Movistar another 11 seconds back and Britain's Oscar Onley of Netcompany-Ineos fifth at 3'45".

The race continues on Thursday with a hilly 177.4km stage from Alcossebre to Castello.
